clue.text: Erotic Ms West about to enter place of debauchery

indicators.note: to enter means the turned-round actress's name goes inside the word for a den of vice

parts.note: a sty is a place of filth and debauchery, as in a pigsty

indicators.note: about tells us the actress's first name is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: Mae West, the Hollywood actress

explanation.surface: Mae West, the saucy film star, wanders into a den of vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ms West' is the Hollywood star Mae West; 'about' turns her name round before it enters the sty.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something steamy is sexually charged, hot and racy.

clue.text: Stone is part of such supports

definitions.meaning: Stone is a town in Staffordshire
poles or sticks used to lean on

explanation.surface: A stone forms part of some supporting structure.
explanation.walkthrough: Stone looks like the material but is a market town in the English county of Staffordshire, commonly abbreviated Staffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking sticks and poles held for support are staffs; the county abbreviation is the other reading.

clue.text: Brought into line, punished, I squealed

indicators.note: punished suggests the letters of the confession are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A culprit, punished, owns up to squealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: things made level or equal have been brought into line with each other.

clue.text: Russian statesman in old group in initiative that ignores English

indicators.note: in places the old group within the shortened word for initiative
that ignores means the letter for English is dropped from the word

parts.note: making the first move is taking the initiative
a lot is a group or batch, as at an auction

explanation.surface: A Russian statesman belongs to an old faction that takes no English initiative.
explanation.walkthrough: The old group goes inside the shortened initiative just after its first letter. Vyacheslav Molotov was Stalin's foreign minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Molotov was the Soviet foreign minister who gave his name to the cocktail.

clue.text: Type of fiction everybody absorbs now — a sign of wintry times

indicators.note: absorbs means the abbreviated fiction genre takes the word now inside it

parts.note: SF stands for science fiction
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A genre of fiction, read by everyone now, signals a cold season.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fall of snow is a typical sign of the winter season.

clue.text: Heavenly body nature's torn apart

indicators.note: apart tells us the letters are pulled to pieces and rearranged

explanation.surface: A celestial object rips nature apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a collapsed star made of densely packed neutrons is a celestial object.

clue.text: Little person with leg obscured in dark coverings?

parts.note: wee means little

indicators.note: obscured means the cricket word for leg is hidden away, removed from the word person

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A small person's leg is hidden beneath dark clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side, so leg gives ON; removing it from PERSON leaves PERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Crape bands or veils worn by mourners were called weepers, black garments of grief.

clue.text: Group of sailors may have put on a party dress

indicators.note: may have put on places the sailors after, tacked onto, the party

parts.note: a do is a party
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A crew of sailors dresses up for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dress something is to decorate or ornament it, as with a dressed shop window.

clue.text: One following advice lets rein slacken

indicators.note: slacken suggests the letters loosen and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A rider taking advice lets the reins go loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who heeds advice hears and attends to it, so is one who pays attention to it.

clue.text: Stars seen in water in ancient Rome looking across one lake

indicators.note: looking across means the Latin word for water stretches around the next letters

parts.note: aqua is Latin for water
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Stars reflected in the water of ancient Rome, seen across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Eagle is a constellation, a named group of stars.

clue.text: Many will show common sense stifling hesitation after hesitation

indicators.note: stifling means the word for common sense smothers the hesitations inside it

parts.note: nous is common sense

indicators.note: after places one hesitation following the other

parts.note: um is a hesitation
er is another hesitation

explanation.surface: Lots of hesitating can smother good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: numerous things are many in number.

clue.text: Sort of employee that's fiddled till — about that get angry, right?

indicators.note: about means the word for get angry goes round the scrambled till

parts.note: to fume is to get angry

indicators.note: fiddled suggests the letters of till are tampered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker who has fiddled the till faces an angry boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled till sits inside the angry word, just after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker employed for a full working week rather than part of it is this kind of employee.

clue.text: Naughty movies — such I found to be perverted

indicators.note: perverted suggests the letters are twisted out of their proper order

explanation.surface: Someone finds naughty films corrupting.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: mischievous behaviour is naughty or playfully troublesome.

clue.text: Computer gear — in time odd bits will go missing

indicators.note: odd bits will go missing means the first, third, fifth letters are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Computer gear goes missing bit by bit over time.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the machine that picks the winning numbers for British Premium Bonds, a government savings lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: ERNIE is a famous random-number machine, a kind of computer.

clue.text: Made to look silly in cafe — even so, ass avoids humiliation

indicators.note: made to look silly suggests the letters are reworked into a ridiculous jumble

explanation.surface: Someone made a fool of in a cafe still escapes embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: keeping your dignity in an awkward moment is what this phrase describes.

clue.text: A fellow meeting religious woman full of love? Writer is one

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

indicators.note: full of means the religious woman holds the zero letter inside

parts.note: a nun is a religious woman
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A man meets a loving nun; a writer is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is a word that names one who does something, built from a verb: a grammatical example, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar term: a noun formed to denote the doer of an action, like writer from write.

clue.text: Settled with supportive funding, is going into hiding

indicators.note: going into hiding means the word is vanishes from the longer word

parts.note: subsidised means backed by financial support

explanation.surface: Someone settled with financial support goes into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ground or sediment that has subsided has sunk down and settled.

clue.text: Merry footsie may be played here

definitions.meaning: merry here means so drunk one has slid to the floor
footsie, flirting with feet, happens beneath the dining surface, out of sight

explanation.surface: Tipsy flirting with feet goes on beneath the dinner table.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being drunk enough to collapse is being under the table, which is also literally where footsie happens.

clue.text: Artist with suggestion that involves a competitive lifestyle

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a trace is a hint or suggestion

explanation.surface: An artist hints at the cut-throat lifestyle.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the endless fierce struggle for success at work is the rat race.

clue.text: I shamble around concealing a deformity

indicators.note: around suggests the letters shuffle about, with the a they conceal set aside

explanation.surface: Someone shuffles about hiding a physical defect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing a' means the A of I SHAMBLE is held back: the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a blemish is a flaw or defect that mars appearance.

clue.text: Young bird that's cold still round garden's borders

indicators.note: round means the word still goes around the edges of the garden

parts.note: yet means still

indicators.note: borders means only the outside letters of garden are used

explanation.surface: A young bird, still cold, waddles round the garden's edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a young swan is called a cygnet.

clue.text: Port wasted, one litre being knocked over

indicators.note: being knocked over means the pair for one and litre are turned round within the word

parts.note: spilt milk is wasted
I is one, L is litre

explanation.surface: Port is wasted when a litre is knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: Port looks like the drink but is the Croatian seaport; 'being knocked over' flips IL in SPILT to LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Split is a seaport on Croatia's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Doesn't have to be careless in speech

indicators.note: in speech signals that the word for careless is heard, spoken

parts.note: lax means careless or slack

explanation.surface: Someone who has nothing to be careless about when speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to lack something is not to have it.

clue.text: Composer, good person to have in cathedral city, showing serious intent

indicators.note: to have in means the cathedral city holds the composer and saint inside

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
Thomas Arne, the English composer of Rule, Britannia
ST, short for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: A composer and a saint in a cathedral city mean business.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: acting earnestly is acting with sincere, serious intent.

clue.text: Duke commanding rubbish soldiers may be one who brooks no opposition

parts.note: I/C means in charge, commanding
tat is cheap rubbish
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers

explanation.surface: A duke commanding useless troops may be a tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an autocrat who rules absolutely tolerates no opposition.

clue.text: Complaint about home of an earlier civilisation

indicators.note: about means the complaint wraps round the word for home

parts.note: a moan is a complaint
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the home of an ancient people.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Bronze Age culture of ancient Crete is the Minoan civilisation.

clue.text: Give out, as Sir Patrick in decline

indicators.note: in places the knight's surname inside the word for decline

parts.note: to die away is to decline
Sir Patrick Spens, hero of a Scottish ballad

explanation.surface: Handing out, as a knight in decline might.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Patrick Spens is the doomed sea captain of a traditional Scottish ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dispense is to distribute or give out.

clue.text: King's companion, traveller originally from Kent district

parts.note: a thane was an Anglo-Saxon nobleman serving the king

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of traveller is taken

explanation.surface: A king's comrade and a traveller come originally from a Kent area.
explanation.walkthrough: Thanet is a district at the north-east tip of Kent, a county of south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Isle of Thanet is a local government district in Kent.
